name: industry_timing

coverage.role: Missing-classification control; retain original static industry labels for stocks and ETFs, but require the contemporaneous source release to contain the stock.
coverage.comparison: Against unchanged local-gap baseline: quantify the eligibility filter and its downstream ranks, labels, calibration, fitting and portfolio effects.

static.role: Retrospective taxonomy/source control, never a deployable strategy. Use the latest archived stock division at every historically covered row, on the same dated coverage mask.
static.comparison: Against coverage: quantify classification source, granularity, as-of membership and stock/ETF grouping changes together; do not call this a pure timing or alpha effect.

dated.role: Use the stock division from the latest catalogue release strictly before the session, on the same coverage mask.
dated.comparison: Against static: isolate published division changes and their date boundaries with identical eligibility, raw data, labels and non-industry ranks.

classification.stock_level: Published division; stable key capco:<section><two-digit division>. No level selected using returns; retain all original labels and evidence separately.
classification.availability: For this explicitly retrospective convention, each release becomes usable at 00:00 Asia/Shanghai on the first observed session strictly after its catalogue date. No same-day use, statistical-period backdating, future-table fill or carrying a stock omitted from a later release.
classification.clock: Features, labels' signal grouping and close-time allocation use information available by 16:00 on the signal date. Actual opening constraints use the classification available by 09:25 on execution day. A release between these times cannot rewrite the frozen close-time intention.
classification.identity: Join exact source security codes, then only the documented one-to-one aliases. Reject ambiguous direct/alias matches. Identity correspondence does not imply historical market membership or eligibility.
classification.unknown_stock: No classification before the first containing release, or when omitted from the latest release. Exclude such stock rows from eligibility before cross-sectional ranks, market breadth, calibration, model fitting and forecast construction. Never use a unique synthetic industry or fall back to the current static label.
classification.unknown_holding: If an existing holding loses classification at an information boundary, stop that research account or paper resolution with an explicit source-data error. Preserve partial evidence; do not fabricate liquidation, carry a prior category, or report the account as complete. Current source joins have no previously covered stock disappearing, but synthetic tests must cover it.
classification.etfs: Keep the same 22 ETFs and original static thematic labels in all comparisons. They are outside CAPCO company classification and remain historically unverified. CAPCO stock keys are separate from ETF labels; the static bridge includes loss of old stock/ETF label coincidences, so category replacement is not claimed to preserve economic sector exposure.
classification.shared_mask: All three variants use only contemporaneous source coverage. The latest-table static control must have a category for every historically covered stock; otherwise stop the control instead of adding a future-dependent eligibility mask.
classification.passive_reclassification: Retain the existing rebalance schedule and exit rules. Reclassification alone does not trigger forced trades. Every new buy must satisfy current opening-time groups and unchanged post-fee caps; record passive concentration after group changes without calling it a new purchase violation.

snapshot_checks: Before editing the numerical path, rebuild the entire active parent with the registered old source and compare every original table field, panel, score, action and metadata value exactly.

Rebuild all three variants from the same raw bars, actions and reviewed statuses. Keep calendar, original metadata fields, price-only panels, raw bars, actions and opening status exact; add only source-bound industry history and provenance metadata.

The common eligibility change must match the independently derived 245 eligible rows across seven stocks. Rebuild all affected ranks, scores and breadth; retain exact labels for every still-eligible row and keep removed-row label status explicit.

All variants must have identical eligibility, non-industry features, raw panels, scores and labels. Only classification groups and industry features differ between variants. Report all differences against the parent separately.

Independently derive every date/security classification from original extracted cells and alias evidence, including before-first-release, publication boundaries, missing rows, source revisions and future-prefix invariance. Do not verify the mapping by reusing its production lookup.
implementation_tests: Reproduce the static-label leakage and opening/closing group inconsistency before changing the affected paths.

Cover same-day exclusion, holiday-delayed availability, late classification changes, omitted stocks, unknown holdings, stable aliases, ETF scope and no look-ahead under source truncation or future perturbation.

Validate grouping in residual targets, prediction neutralization, factor gates, allocation, post-fill caps, paper resolution and independent account audit. Opening group changes must not rewrite the preceding close's intention.

Keep absence of industry history byte-compatible with all frozen legacy models, accounts and paper records. Include the new dependency in experiment and paper source identities; never bypass ordinary stale-source guards.
Support isolated registered experiment configurations without editing the active project configuration during comparisons. Reject escaping configuration paths and mixed dataset/model identities.

compatibility.scope: Explicit diagnostics on the unchanged baseline input. All numerical arrays, selections, ledgers and accounting must match; normal stale-source checks remain enabled.

fixed_forecast_diagnostics.coverage: Baseline forecasts on the coverage variant, dropping only now-ineligible symbol/date keys; do not recalibrate. Compare with baseline and fully retrained coverage accounts.
fixed_forecast_diagnostics.static: Coverage forecasts on the static variant, requiring identical eligible row identities. Compare with retrained static results.
fixed_forecast_diagnostics.dated: Static forecasts on the dated variant, requiring identical eligible row identities. Compare with retrained dated results.
fixed_forecast_diagnostics.scope: Separately labelled attribution only. Never pass mismatched-source models through the ordinary evaluation path or present fixed forecasts as retrained predictions.

attribution: Report selected strategy and same-input, same-risk momentum for every variant, all three costs, full continuous net return, drawdown, reset 10-session means, turnover, fees, blocked buys, passive reclassification exposure and every quality flag. Report per-window selections and full failures, not only the best row.
risk: Balanced attack, 8 percent warning, original high-water mark and latched non-recovering state. Existing allocation caps, post-fee purchase caps, liquidity, lots, costs and turnover rules unchanged. Benchmarks use the same classification and information-time convention as each compared strategy.
budget: No additional alpha candidates, parameter tuning, recovery variants or looser adoption gates. These three registered data controls are not a return-selected search.
adoption: Coverage and static are attribution controls. Dated may become a new retrospective research baseline only after all registered data, compatibility, training, independent ledger, paper and historical-status checks pass, irrespective of return direction. Exact historical publication and ETF availability remain uncertified, and no superiority or forward-performance claim follows from engineering checks. Freeze a newly source-bound paper plan only after a validated active configuration exists; never re-date or overwrite an older plan.
limitations: Current-universe and survivorship selection remain; source completeness is not historical universe membership.
Catalogue publication times and historical file bytes are not independently certified. All dated results must state the retrospective availability convention.
ETF thematic labels, 111 other quote-gap endpoints, unresolved corporate-action fields and repeated quality flags remain explicit.
Competition whitepaper remains authoritative; fee and matching details remain unconfirmed. No trading app, broker account or WeChat actions.
